original_text: \cite{Greisen:1966jv,Zatsepin:1966jv} limit of $E\sim 5\times 10^{19}$ eV (or GZK cutoff) is the upper bound on the   energy for a   cosmic ray protons traveling from their production in very distant galaxies through the intergalactic medium to us.
injected_text: \cite{Greisen:1966jv,Zatsepin:1966jv} limit of $E\sim 5\times 10^{19}$ eV (or GZK cutoff) is the lower bound on the   energy for a   cosmic ray protons traveling from their production in very distant galaxies through the intergalactic medium to us.
rationale: Direction reversal of cited conclusion. Greisen (1966) and Zatsepin & Kuzmin (1966) — the founding papers on the GZK cutoff (cite keys preserved byte-for-byte) — establish that the cutoff is the UPPER bound on the energy of cosmic ray protons that can survive intergalactic propagation. Reversing 'upper bound' → 'lower bound' contradicts the physics of the GZK process (proton energy degradation by CMB photons via pion production) and contradicts the cited papers' stated result.
ground_truth_description: Polarity flip of the GZK-cutoff direction claim: 'upper bound' → 'lower bound'. Greisen 1966 + Zatsepin-Kuzmin 1966 establish the GZK as an UPPER bound on cosmic-ray-proton energies above ~5×10^19 eV; the injected sentence reverses the direction.

rationale: Wrong-but-plausible formula. The Dirac monopole charge in Gaussian units is g₀ = e/(2α) where α is the fine-structure constant (so g/e = 1/(2α) ≈ 68.5, giving g ≈ 3.3×10^-8 esu). Replacing with g = 2eα flips the relationship: the injected formula gives g ≈ 7×10^-12 esu (4 orders of magnitude smaller than the stated value 3.3×10^-8). Wolfram refutes by symbolic comparison against the canonical Dirac quantization e·g = ℏc/2 (Gaussian) → g = ℏc/(2e) = e/(2α).
ground_truth_description: Replaced the canonical Dirac monopole charge formula 'g = e/(2α)' with the structurally similar but algebraically wrong 'g = 2eα'. The numerical value '3.3×10^-8 esu' (correct for the original formula) is preserved, creating an internal inconsistency between formula and value.
